items.title: 67256_Paul L. Howard oral history interview
items.q: When he took that thing out, and a fellow by the name of Buster Wilson was playing the piano... Well, I played blues... And so Dink was standing there... and it was called a cornet at that time... and at one part of the thing I was playing and something said (Singing) -- and that was Ernest coming i

ctx.x: all through the piece, and I played all of Victor Herbert's numbers, trumpet solos -- cornet, it wasn't trumpet, it was cornet. Triple-tonguing, double-tonguing, triple-tonguing and all that, I did all of that. Those Italians had taught me how to do that. And you'd be surprised. When he took that thing out, and a fellow by the name of Buster Wilson was playing the piano, and started playing -- oh, Buster, Buster just started playing the blues, you know, just ordinary blues.
